records.candidate_title_fr: Bénédiction de la maison à l'Épiphanie
records.action_identity: Priest performs a specified Epiphany house blessing, including prayer, sprinkling with holy water, and incensation. A household's devotional chalk inscription is associated but must not be represented as the same ministerial rite.

main_identity_comparison.reason: Epiphany star singers, King's Cake and general household use of holy water are not the specified Epiphany house-blessing rite.

sources.where: Original printed p149, PDF zero-index 166; Blessing of Homes
sources.finding: Describes a pastor giving the blessing, including Magnificat, sprinkling, incensing, prayers and chalk

sources.where: Philip Weller, Roman Ritual Volume III, 1952, Epiphany house blessing
sources.finding: Provides distinguishable priestly formulary with antiphon, Magnificat, sprinkling and incensation
Describes separate practice of chalk inscription, C+M+B, and its significance

calendar_target.suggested_day: 6 January (1962 Calendar resolver owns the feast)
calendar_target.geographical_scope: Historical Latin-rite custom, no universal parish availability asserted
calendar_target.display_category: Optional local rite and related household custom

records.draft_en: At Epiphany some Catholic households invite their priest to bless the home, recalling Christ's manifestation to the nations. The older Roman Ritual contains a special blessing with the Magnificat, prayers, holy water and incense. Marking the doorway with chalk is a related household tradition, but it must not be confused with the priest's rite. Availability depends on local clergy and practice.
records.draft_fr: À l'Épiphanie, certaines familles catholiques invitent un prêtre à bénir leur maison, en mémoire de la manifestation du Christ aux nations. L'ancien Rituel romain prévoit une bénédiction particulière avec le Magnificat, des prières, de l'eau bénite et de l'encens. L'inscription à la craie sur la porte est une coutume domestique associée, distincte du rite accompli par le prêtre. Sa célébration dépend des usages et des prêtres du lieu.
records.suggested_prayer_owner: Reference the authoritative historical Ritual only after rubric/text rights and 1962 applicability are confirmed; do not fabricate domestic priestly formulas.

records.candidate_title_en: Taking Easter light home after the Vigil
records.candidate_title_fr: Rapporter la lumière pascale à la maison
records.action_identity: Some Catholic households take a light kindled at Easter from church to their home in a lantern or candle; distinguished from the priestly blessing of fire in the vigil itself and from Easter food blessings.

main_identity_comparison.reason: BLSS-004 concerns blessed Easter foods; EAST-001 is an Emmaus walk. Neither owns domestic carriage of the Easter light.

sources.where: Original printed p217, PDF zero-index 234; Easter Vigil blessed fire carried in lanterns
sources.finding: Describes taking blessed-fire flames home in lanterns and lighting a vigil lamp

sources.where: How to Make Your House a Home, 1955 / New Fire of Easter
sources.finding: Describes a family bringing light in a lantern after the vigil, subject to parish permission
Notes taking Easter light home is customary in many Austrian regions

calendar_target.suggested_day: Holy Saturday Vigil; date from existing Calendar
calendar_target.geographical_scope: Documented some European regions, with Austria as modern diocesan witness

records.draft_en: In some European Catholic communities, families carry the light of Easter home after the Vigil, traditionally using a protected lantern to light a lamp before the crucifix. It recalls the risen Christ as the Light of the World. This is a household custom, not an additional part of the Mass; it depends on local parish arrangements and fire-safety rules.
records.draft_fr: Dans certaines régions catholiques d'Europe, les familles rapportent chez elles la lumière de Pâques après la Vigile, autrefois dans une lanterne protégée, afin d'allumer une lampe près du crucifix. Ce geste rappelle le Christ ressuscité, Lumière du monde. Il s'agit d'une coutume familiale, et non d'un rite supplémentaire de la messe ; elle dépend des usages paroissiaux et des règles de sécurité.
